texts.facts: The petitioner is aggrieved by the fourth respondent's orders seizing the R.O. water units under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the Act'). It is undisputed that the Mohaddis-E-Azam Mission vs Joint Director (Regulatory ... on 20 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140005982/ 2 fourth respondent has initiated the aforesaid proceeding for seizure because the petitioner has not obtained necessary certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
texts.arguments: 2 The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has setup R.O. water plant on a non- profitable basis. The water from the R.O. water plant is available to the poorer section of the society in the locality free of cost and not as packaged water. The plant has been set up after securing clarification from the concerned as per Annexure - A. The certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards would be required only when water is sold as packaged drinking water, but if the facility is set up for distributing water in cans for the benefit of the community, such certification would not be required. 3 A Division Bench of this Court in Lochamesh B Hugar v. Union of India and others reported in (2013) 2 KLJ 643, relying upon the provisions of Food and Safety Standards (Food Products, Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, more specifically regulation 2.10.8, has directed the Authorities to ensure that all necessary steps are taken to prohibit, prevent, manufacture and sale of packaged drinking water without certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards with further directions. The amendment reads as follows: "2.10.8 Packaged Drinking Water (other than mineral water) - 1. means water, other than natural water that is likely to be used for human consumption and that is offered or sold in packaged form, by whatever name it may be called, offered or sold."
